items.stem: A laptop is seized powered on and connected to the network. What should the responder capture first?

options.text: Volatile data such as memory and active network connections
options.rationale: Correct: volatile data is lost on power-off, so it is captured before imaging the disk.

options.text: A printout of the installed software list
options.rationale: Non-volatile and low priority compared to volatile data.

options.text: The disk image, after shutting the machine down
options.rationale: Shutting down first destroys volatile evidence.

items.explanation: Correct: volatile data is lost on power-off, so it is captured before imaging the disk.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which two practices preserve the integrity of acquired disk evidence? (Select TWO)

options.text: Using a write blocker during acquisition
options.rationale: Correct: a write blocker prevents changes to the source.

options.text: Recording a cryptographic hash of the image and re-verifying it
options.rationale: Correct: matching hashes prove the image was not altered.

options.text: Editing the image to remove irrelevant files first
options.rationale: Editing the image destroys its integrity.

options.text: Storing the only copy on the suspect's own machine
options.rationale: That risks loss and tampering of the evidence.

items.explanation: Correct: a write blocker prevents changes to the source.; Correct: matching hashes prove the image was not altered.

items.stem: Why should a forensic report distinguish observed facts from the investigator's inferences?

options.text: Because conclusions must be supported by evidence and open to challenge
options.rationale: Correct: separating fact from inference keeps the report defensible and honest.
Inferences can be reasonable; they just must be labelled.

options.text: Because facts are not allowed in reports
options.rationale: Facts are the core of the report.

options.text: Because the chain of custody replaces the need for analysis
options.rationale: Chain of custody supports but does not replace analysis.

items.explanation: Correct: separating fact from inference keeps the report defensible and honest.
